text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Polish flag-carrier PLL LOT reported a net loss of 47 million zlotys last year, and its gross loss was 41 million zlotys. The airline's costs were 1.52 billion zlotys and revenues reached 1.48 billion zlotys showing a 29 percent growth compared with the 1995 results.
- Around 23 percent of Poland's manufacturing firms said the industrial climate last year was good, while 13 percent found it bad, a survey by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) showed.
- Volkswagen's Poznan plant will daily assemble 20 VW Polo cars by the end of March, VW Poznan director Adam Dobielinski said. VW dealers have already contracted sales of 5,000 Polos.

- Provincial representatives of Turin and Piedmont opened a Piedmont business information desk at the National Chamber of Commerce (KIG) in Warsaw to promote business cooperation between Poland and northern Italy.

- Plus GSM digital mobile phone operator, controlled by Polkomtel, has already contracted 100,000 subscribers. Its digital telecom competitor, Era GSM, has contracted 80,000 subscribers, whereas the Centertel analogue mobile phone firm, controlled by Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecom monopolist, has 160,000 subscribers.

- Polish-Japanese trade exchange was $635.1 million in 1996, and Japanese investments in Poland totalled $32.45 million, making Japan the twentieth biggest investor, Matsushita Battery Poland president Nobuyako Kobayoshi said.

- Gerlach cutlery maker earned a net profit of 549,400 zlotys on revenues of 36.3 million zlotys in 1996. This year's net profit will account for six percent of revenues, Gerlach's board president Krzysztof Kurzawa said.

- The general shareholders' meeting of the Bank Rozwoju Cukrownictwa (BRC) sugar sector development bank have decided on a new share issue of 15.2 million zlotys to increase the bank's owned funds to 35 million zlotys.
NOWA EUROPA

- Poland's banking regulations are too restrictive and blunt the country's competitiveness, Polish Banking Association (ZBA) general director Krzysztof Pietraszkiewicz said. The finance ministry as well as the central bank agree parliament should change the banking law as soon as possible.
- Korea's Daewoo concern is planning to build a vehicle lamp and lighting equipment plant in northeastern Poland, Centrum Daewoo president Jung Ho Choi said.
- Polish Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek has gone on an official visit to Germany, invited by the German Economy Minister Guenter Rexrodt.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Kredyt Bank is planning to credit 23 million zlotys to finance production of a historical movie based on a book by Henryk Sienkiewicz, to be directed by Jerzy Hoffman. The budget will be the biggest in the history of Poland's film industry.
ZYCIE
- Polish-German trade exchange was $17.5 billion last year which made Poland Germany's biggest trade partner in central and eastern Europe.
- The number of cash dispensers accepting VISA cards in Poland will grow to 800 by January next year, VISA said.
PARKIET
- The Olkusz-based Emalia Olkusz cooking pot maker will make a net profit of four million zlotys against a 9.5 million zlotys net loss last year, the company forecast said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
